parsed.narrative: With the default choices, religiosity goes with higher well-being: beta = 0.140 (95% CI 0.119 to 0.160), p < 0.001, n = 10,535, so the verdict is POSITIVE ASSOCIATION. Borges ran 38 universes: the baseline, 13 single changes and 24 combinations. No flip was found: all 38 universes keep the verdict (design-weighted robustness 100%); the estimate runs from 0.060 to 0.150, the lowest interval bound is 0.043 and the largest p-value is p < 0.001. The 110 research teams that reported a standardised effect range from 0.007 to 0.354 (median 0.120), and 110 of them (100%) have an interval above zero.
caveats: The robustness figure comes from a uniform random sample of the option grid, which is built from the choices the teams documented; the share among all explored universes leans toward flips because the search chases them. Neither is a population estimate.
Standardised coefficients describe an association in a convenience sample of 24 countries; they do not show that religion causes well-being.
2 universes failed to run and are excluded.
